recordedOnly.note: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31: the gate moves 95 -> 93 and the one-item change from 17206 to 16806 component renders. This is NOT a code change and NOT a regression — nothing about what the grid draws was touched. The number moved with the environment, and the evidence is that it moved WITHOUT the source moving: CI measured 95 at 3233351a and 93 at 21329b43, and the only difference between those two commits is version fields and CHANGELOG text. Checking 3233351a out on a second machine and rebuilding it measured 16806/93 there too — the same commit CI had just scored 95. So 95 was never portable off the machine that captured it; it was pinned as an exact gate on the strength of three runs from ONE build on ONE machine, which cannot distinguish 'deterministic' from 'deterministic here'. Ruled out along the way, each by measurement rather than reasoning: market price data (seeding a frozen snapshot into the flavor's cache, and separately seeding one with zero entries, both still read 16806/93, and the per-card price control was present either way), and the removal of the nightly flavor (the commit that did it is 3233351a, which CI scored 95). Two component types and ~400 renders — about two per card across ~220 cards — remain unattributed to any input this repo controls. 93 is what both CI and a second machine now measure, so it is what the gate records; if a third environment disagrees, the honest conclusion is that this field cannot be gated exactly and should stop being, rather than that someone regressed it. The instrument now uploads its capture as a CI artifact so the next disagreement can be diffed component by component instead of re-investigated from a bare number. Re-measured from scratch after the instrument moved off the deleted Planning screen and onto Inventory. Everything below is a NEW baseline against a different screen and a different fixture (account-offline: 13 heroes, 221 items) — it is not comparable to the figures this file carried before, and nothing here is a regression against them. A quiet window still costs ZERO, unchanged and for the same reason: the fixture ticker's ~100 commits per 5s all carry an identical body, so no account:changed is emitted at all. The one-item change is dropping a single gear item, which costs 17206 component renders across 8 commits and touches 95 distinct component types — two orders of magnitude above what the old two-hero Planning roster cost, because the grid re-renders all ~220 cards and their per-card subtrees for a change to one of them. That is a real, pre-existing property of the grid this instrument now makes visible; it is not something this move introduced. Three consecutive local runs from one build produced 0/17206/95 every time, byte-identical. The ranges keep a margin for a slower CI machine rather than pinning exact values.
